meta_desc: NCERT Class 12 Maths Integration Exercise 7.11 solved — properties of definite integrals, king property and even/odd rules, with a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Properties of Definite Integrals Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the properties used all through Exercise 7.11 — the king property, even and odd functions, and the 0 to 2a split. Answer each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Properties of definite integrals (NCERT Class 12, Ex 7.11)

questions.q: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx is equal to which of these?
questions.explanation: This is the king property: replacing x by (a − x) leaves the value unchanged over the interval 0 to a. It is the single most-used trick in Exercise 7.11.

questions.q: If f is an odd function, f(−x) = −f(x), what is ∫<sub>−a</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx?
questions.explanation: The area on the negative side cancels the area on the positive side, so the integral of any odd function over a symmetric interval is 0.

questions.q: If f is an even function, f(−x) = f(x), then ∫<sub>−a</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx equals:
questions.explanation: An even function is symmetric about the y-axis, so the two halves are equal and the integral is twice the value from 0 to a.

questions.q: Using the king property, evaluate ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> sin x / (sin x + cos x) dx.
questions.explanation: Call the integral I. Replacing x by (π/2 − x) swaps sin and cos, giving a second integral with cos on top. Adding the two makes the integrand 1, so 2I = π/2, hence I = π/4.
sin<sup>3</sup>x is an odd function and the limits are symmetric, so the integral is 0 — no calculation of the antiderivative needed.

questions.q: ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(x) dx can be rewritten as:
questions.explanation: The general king property over [a, b] replaces x by (a + b − x). The special case a = 0 gives the familiar f(a − x) form.

questions.q: Which identity correctly splits ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2a</sup> f(x) dx?
questions.explanation: Split the interval at a; on the second piece substitute x = 2a − t. This gives ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> [f(x) + f(2a − x)] dx, the standard 0-to-2a property.

questions.q: For a positive integer n, the value of ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/2</sup> sin<sup>n</sup>x / (sin<sup>n</sup>x + cos<sup>n</sup>x) dx is:
questions.explanation: The same king-property pairing as the sin/cos question works for any power n: adding I to its (π/2 − x) version gives 2I = π/2, so I = π/4 regardless of n.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.11 of NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It is built entirely around the properties of definite integrals — the king property ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(a+b−x) dx, the even and odd function rules over symmetric limits, and the 0-to-2a split. Most questions are solved by choosing the right property before integrating.

faq.q: What is the 'king property' of definite integrals?
faq.a: It says ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>a</sup> f(a−x) dx, or more generally ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(x) dx = ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(a+b−x) dx. It turns awkward trigonometric integrals into ones you can add to the original and solve in two lines.

faq.q: How do even and odd functions make these integrals easier?
faq.a: Over a symmetric interval from −a to a, an odd function integrates to 0 and an even function integrates to twice its value from 0 to a. Spotting the symmetry first often removes the need to find an antiderivative at all.

faq.q: Do I still need to memorise antiderivatives for Exercise 7.11?
faq.a: Yes. The properties reduce the work, but you finish most problems with a standard integral — powers of sin and cos, or basic algebraic forms — so the earlier exercises in Chapter 7 still matter here.
